Si ésta es la única o la última. sweep_summary: Four title-keyword items for Paraguayan Guaraní (para1311, catalog: fixed-strict final on StressTyp2/Ayala 1993). Three are Glottolog machine mis-assignments (lgcode 'computerized assignment from "prosa"/"verso"' on the Glottolog reference pages): Düwel 1978 (Slavic prose rhythm), Caputo & D'Imperio 1995 (Italian prosodic transcription), Funke 1962 (Old English homiletic prose) — not relevant, priority none. The only real item, Clopper & Tonhauser 2013 IJAL (focus prosody; already listed), has no open copy (S2 CLOSED, Unpaywall/OpenAlex not OA, no abstract in any index, UChicago and JSTOR bot-walled, author sites link only the DOI) — paywalled-doi, priority medium. Its 2011 WCCFL precursor (author preprint already on file, provenance re-checked against Tonhauser's pubs-by-year page) was read: canonical stress is word-final, but lexical exceptions (óga) and non-stress-attracting suffixes (-ta, -ma) yield penult/antepenult word stress, and the experiment itself used final/penult/antepenult-stressed verbs — refines the strict-final coding toward final-default with morphological conditioning, consistent with the prior audit's Estigarribia 2020 and Gregores & Suárez 1967 findings and its recode recommendation. Also fetched sources Tonhauser 2019 'Prosody and meaning' handbook chapter (scanned, general; not a Guaraní stress source). discovery used author pages, S2/Unpaywall/OpenAlex/Crossref/CORE APIs and Glottolog pages.

new_statements.quote: The canonical position for lexical stress is the final syllable of the word, in which case it is not orthographically marked; if lexical stress occurs in any other position or is associated with a nasal vowel, it is marked by an acute accent or a tilde, respectively (e.g., apyka ‘chair’, óga ‘house’, hatã ‘hard’). Some suffixes attract lexical stress and others do not: the desiderative modal suffix –se ‘DES’, for example, attracts lexical stress (e.g., a-ha-se [...] ‘I want to go’, not *a-há-se), whereas the prospective aspect/modal marker –ta ‘PROSP’ and the perfect aspect marker –ma ‘PERFECT’ do not

new_statements.reading: Final stress is the canonical (default, orthographically unmarked) position; lexically non-final roots exist (óga) and common unstressed suffixes (-ta, -ma) regularly leave word stress on the penult or antepenult, while stress-attracting suffixes (-se) pull it to the end. This is a morphologically conditioned final-default system, not exceptionless word-final stress — the same picture the prior audit drew from Estigarribia 2020 (sec. 2.2.2) and Gregores & Suárez 1967 (sec. 5.141), and the same system the catalog codes 'morphological' for Kaiwá, Guajá and Tapirapé. It refines/contradicts the 'fixed-strict final' coding built on the truncated StressTyp2/Ayala 1993 passage.

The canonical position for lexical stress is the final syllable of the word, in which case it is not orthographically marked; if lexical stress occurs in any other position or is associated with a nasal vowel, it is marked by an acute accent or a tilde, respectively (e.g., apyka ‘chair’, óga ‘house’, hatã ‘hard’). sources.locator: author preprint PDF p.3 of 9 (proceedings pagination 249-257 per Clopper's CV, so approx. p.251; the preprint carries no printed page numbers), section 2 background paragraph on lexical stress
sources.note: Word-final stress is the canonical/default position (unmarked in orthography); non-final stress exists lexically (óga 'house') and arises regularly from non-stress-attracting suffixes (-ta PROSP, -ma PERFECT: a-há-ta, a-há-ma vs. stress-attracting -se: a-ha-se). The experiment deliberately built verbs with final, penultimate and antepenultimate stress (root + -ma, root + -ta-ma), i.e. the authors treat non-final word stress as productive. This refines the catalog's fixed-strict final coding toward 'final by default, morphologically conditioned', in line with the held Estigarribia 2020 and Gre…

sources.quote: 'At least one of the last three syllables must include primary stress, most normally the last one or the last but one: the former is the case in a much larger number of different macrosegments, though the text-frequency of the latter is not particularly low; on the contrary, both the total frequency and the text-frequency of proparoxytonic macrosegments is very low.' Loanwords mostly adapted 'with stress in the last syllable, no matter in which syllable the stress originally fell'.

sources.quote: 'PG has lexical stress, typically on the last syllable of a lexical item. However, because many suffixes do not have stress, stress can be on the penult or antepenult of a prosodic word. When a stressed suffix is added, stress shifts to the suffix, and when multiple suffixes have stress, stress shifts to the last stressed suffix (cf. o-karú, o-karú-ta, o-karú-ta-ma, o-karu-pá, o-karu-pa-sé.)' Note 9: 'Guarani roots are to a great extent stress final (the unmarked case), but when an unstressed suffix is attached to it, stress appears on the penultimate syllable of the root [sic].'
